deep.reconstruction:
Context: these are preparatory notes for Grothendieck's Nov–Dec 1967 IHES lectures 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes'. The next page is the lecture plan; its §6 'Calculs Čechistes' corresponds to §6 of the published notes taken by J. Coates and O. Jussila (in Dix exposés, 1968). The previous page announces the goal: attach to any quasi-coherent F a stratified pro-module Q°(F) whose stratifying cohomology is the ordinary Zariski cohomology of F. Q°(F) should be functorial in differential operators, so that the Zariski hypercohomology of a complex of differential operators becomes the stratifying cohomology of a complex of stratified sheaves.

Setup on this page:
- P^i is the pro-ring of functions on the formal neighbourhood of the diagonal in X^{i+1} (X^{i+1} = fibre product over S). So P^* is a cosimplicial pro-ring with P^0 = O_X and P^1 = P^∞_{X/S}, the infinite-order principal parts.
- Q^* = (SP)^* is the shifted (décalé) cosimplicial object, Q^i = P^{i+1}.
- α^·: P^* → Q^* is the extra coface. It makes Q^* a cosimplicial algebra over P^*.
- For a module M, set Q^{i-1}[M] = P^i ⊗_{O_X} M, the pro-module of (i-fold) principal parts of M.

Claim on the page. A differential operator D: M → N relative to S (of finite order n) is the same as a linear map P^n ⊗ M → N. Hence it induces maps P^i ⊗ M → P^i ⊗ N. These maps are not P^i-linear. They are only P^{i-1}-linear, where P^i ⊗ M is viewed as a P^{i-1}-module by restriction of scalars along α^{i-1}: P^{i-1} → P^i.

So M ↦ Q^{i-1}[M] is a functor from (O_X-modules, differential operators rel. S) to P^{i-1}-modules. In particular Q^0[M] = P^1 ⊗ M is a functor from (O_X-modules with differential operators rel. S) to pro-O_X-modules. Q^0[M] carries a natural stratification (the HPD/infinite-order linearization). Its stratifying (crystalline, char 0) cohomology recovers the Zariski cohomology of M.

The last lines begin to transfer the cosimplicial algebra structure to 'exterior operations', i.e. cup products / module structures on the resulting Čech complexes. The page breaks off there.

In modern terms, this is the linearization of differential operators. It is the functor L(M) = P^∞ ⊗ M from modules with differential operators to crystals. It underlies the comparison: de Rham complex Ω^• ↦ L(Ω^•), a resolution of O_X in crystals, giving H_crys(X/S, O) ≅ H_dR(X/S).
errors: The precise sense in which a finite-order differential operator induces a map on the full pro-object P^i⊗M is left implicit. One must pass to the pro-system, using P^{n+m} → P^n ⊗ P^m (composition of operators). This is routine.

In the boxed side remark, the identification 'P^i[M] considered as P^{i-1}-module (or what is the same Q^{i-1}[M])' is index-shifted notation. It is consistent with the footnote Q^{i-1}[M] = P^i ⊗_{O_X} M.

ideas.what: Cosimplicial pro-ring P^* of formal neighbourhoods of diagonals and its shift Q^* = (SP)^*, with α: P^* → Q^* making Q^* a cosimplicial P^*-algebra (Čech–Alexander / décalage set-up for stratifying cohomology).
ideas.modern_name: Čech–Alexander complex / décalage of the cosimplicial infinitesimal neighbourhood (Grothendieck's 'Čech calculations' for the stratifying/infinitesimal site)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas (1968), §§5–7

ideas.what: Q^0[M] = P^∞ ⊗ M as a stratified pro-module, functorial in M with respect to differential operators; Q^{i-1}[M] only P^{i-1}-linear via α.
ideas.modern_name: Linearization of differential operators, L(M) = P^∞_X ⊗ M
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals, 1968); developed by Berthelot (Cohomologie cristalline, 1974) and Berthelot–Ogus
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (1968), comparison of de Rham and crystalline cohomology

ideas.what: Special case: diag X→X×_S X a nilpotent immersion, so stratification = descent data and Q°(F) = f^*f_*F (previous page).
ideas.modern_name: Descent data as stratification for universal homeomorphisms / radicial case

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of the linearization-of-differential-operators construction that appears in Grothendieck's 1968 Crystals notes and was developed systematically by Berthelot. Nothing here goes beyond the published record.
transcription_corrections: 'Q^0[M] est d'un foncteur' should read 'Q^0[M] est donc un foncteur'.
The struck-out boxed line reads roughly '[P^0[M] = M ... ... Ab(X)]' and is cancelled in the original.
'{+algèbre+}' replaces a struck word before 'cosimpliciale'; the next word is probably 'anneau' (written over a struck word), giving 'sur l'anneau cosimplicial P^*'.
The vertical margin text is largely illegible. Readings like 'Anti-Riesz' are doubtful and probably unrelated to the main text, or form a stray note.
